critical_code_review_comments: graph.py: clean. _resolve_graphify() does filesystem probing at request time (not import), so restricted supervisor PATH doesn't break startup — good defense. _graph_lock asyncio.Lock prevents concurrent regraph; second concurrent call returns 409. Staleness scan walks backend + frontend/src and skips node_modules/__pycache__/.venv/graphify-out — fine for current repo size but O(files) per status request; consider caching if repo grows.

graph.py: NODE_TOPOLOGY is referenced inside /doctrine (line 206) but defined AFTER the function (line 213). Python resolves names at call time so this works, but it is a read-order smell — move NODE_TOPOLOGY + REPOS above the /doctrine handler for clarity and to prevent a future refactor from breaking it.

ledger.py: webhook correctly returns 410 for stripe with doctrine-mandated detail string, 400 for unknown sources, accepts square|cloudflare|manual|test. amount_cents→amount_usd conversion and bucket defaulting to 1 (Kids Fund) are clean.

GraphifyMode.js: refresh interval 20s + pause-when-hidden is appropriate; error state surfaces HTTPException detail via e.response.data.detail; regraph button correctly disables during inflight call. Doctrine rendering is dynamic from /api/doctrine — no hardcoded forbidden words in the component, so adding new ones only requires a backend change. Good architecture.
Sidebar Graphify button renders NEW pill via the same conditional block as the other four mission-tone modes — consistent with existing pattern.
CommandPalette: Go to Graphify entry added correctly with Network icon and hint 'Knowledge graph + doctrine'; firing it dispatches onModeChange('graphify'). Clean.

Doctrine sweep: confirmed zero forbidden-word leaks in 8 sampled user-facing API payloads and 6 rendered UI modes. The only places {haiku,payment,payment,,outreach} appear are the explicit doctrine chips (allowed) and the fl_compliance string which intentionally names the banned terms. This satisfies Joshua's FL §496.405 rule.
